title: The AMD HIP port is a valuable backend reference, not an OpenNR runtime candidate

rows.observed: The public HIP source wires preblock, Swin encoder, eight 640-token x 1024-channel ViT blocks, decoder skips, postblock and RGB head; it reports 71 logical blocks.
rows.interpretation: Strong evidence that the repository is an explicit runnable graph scaffold, not only a README or a partial kernel demo.

rows.observed: The converter accepts only the SHA-pinned 310.8.0.0 DLL and records 223 tables, but C32/attention layouts and the ViT bridge are marked AMD-consumer-derived; strict conversion refuses incomplete maps.
rows.interpretation: The graph is useful for experiments, but it is not established NVIDIA numerical equivalence or a verified native teacher.

rows.observed: DLSS5_HIP_TRACE adds one reduction launch per logical block and reports element count, nonfinite count, min, max, sum and a hash after each marked block.
rows.interpretation: Useful compact health and stage-identity telemetry; it does not currently dump intermediate activation tensors for feature distillation.

rows.observed: The V2 C API accepts reset, motion and history, but the live ReShade/vkd3d path calls the frame API with reset=1 and logs that it is not temporal.
rows.interpretation: The repository exposes a temporal experiment surface, not a temporally validated live implementation.

rows.observed: The release reports about 210-216 ms GPU time per 1920x1080 inference on an RX 9070 XT/gfx1201 over three runs.
rows.interpretation: This is a network-only proof-of-concept timing, not in-game FPS, stereo frame time, or headset delivery evidence.

rows.observed: The repository has one public commit and a v0.1.0-poc release; project code is marked MIT, modified vkd3d-proton is LGPL-2.1-or-later, and NVIDIA DLLs/weights are excluded.
rows.interpretation: Source review is feasible, but vendor-derived coefficient and binary terms remain a separate private-use boundary.

source.label: Read-only audit of the public repository and release
filters: No external binary execution or game installation

metricDefinitions.label: Moderate-high confidence
metricDefinitions.definition: The implementation and stated behavior are directly inspectable, but the external performance and equivalence claims were not independently reproduced on this machine.

metricDefinitions.label: Intermediate activation trace
metricDefinitions.definition: A serialized tensor or feature map at a selected graph boundary, not a scalar health summary such as min/max/hash.

caveats: The external source snapshot omits its local regression suites even though the Makefile references them.
No local AMD gfx1201 hardware or ROCm execution was available for independent reproduction.
A public software license does not grant redistribution rights for vendor-derived DLLs, weights or unrelated bundled components.

rows.result: The local 310.8.0.0 carrier has six neural families, 218 entry points, readable PTX/SASS summaries and 71-block structural correspondence.
rows.meaning: Our current RTX branch already has a stronger hardware-local backend reference than an AMD port can provide for the Windows target.

rows.result: The local C32 feed-forward probe reduced a 127.633 ms eager control to 5.477 ms (23.30x); the complete C64 block measured 1.980 ms versus 35.823 ms (18.09x).
rows.meaning: The external HIP result reinforces the existing conclusion that fixed layouts, fused tensor-core kernels and workspace discipline matter more than weight-only conversion.

rows.result: The local recovered full graph remains offline-only; generic compile/export paths failed to produce a usable full runtime, and the representative block-core estimate is still optimistic.
rows.meaning: A 71-block explicit HIP graph does not remove the remaining schedule, parity, stereo, temporal and host-contract work.

rows.result: The recovered MLX-DLSS teacher replay improved some RGB rows but failed the <=0.007 Gate-A requirement, with material per-sequence regressions.
rows.meaning: Neither the local recovered graph nor the AMD-derived layouts should become trusted distillation supervision without a source-matched native parity gate.

rows.result: The primary target is Windows 11, Skyrim VR, Quest 3/OpenXR, RTX 5070 Ti and the exact Feature 18-bound per-eye color/depth/motion/reset path.
rows.meaning: The external Linux/Proton/FidelityFX hook and gfx1201-only bridge do not match the current production or capture ownership boundary.

source.label: Current OpenNR-VR reports and project baseline
filters: Evidence available in the current dirty OpenNR-VR worktree as of 2026-09-13
Offline backend and teacher-parity results only
No live runtime or active profile mutation for this assessment

metricDefinitions.label: Native teacher
metricDefinitions.definition: The actual Skyrim/Open Shaders Feature 18 output from the pinned local 310.8 baseline.

metricDefinitions.label: Offline backend timing
metricDefinitions.definition: A model or subgraph measurement that excludes the full renderer, resource interop, compositor, headset and live temporal contract unless explicitly stated.

caveats: The local repository contains user-owned dirty changes; this report does not claim the worktree is clean.
Local fusion timings are backend-control measurements, not native NVIDIA bit identity or live VR acceptance.

rows.evidence: Explicit HIP source, full graph schedule, ROCm kernel families, strict table validation and a live boundary are inspectable.
rows.decision: Use as a design reference for fixed-layout fusion, block manifests, and ABI/host boundary review.

rows.evidence: The current trace exports scalar reductions and hashes, not activation tensors; the layouts are partly derived and the graph has no training/autograd path.
rows.decision: Do a selected-stage feature probe only in an isolated research lineage, preferably after native first-frame parity improves.

rows.evidence: Derived C32/attention layouts and a derived ViT bridge are explicitly not NVIDIA-equivalent; live history is reset each frame.
rows.decision: Do not replace or relabel the native teacher. Keep promotion=false.

rows.evidence: The release is Linux x86_64, ROCm/HIP 7, gfx1201 and Wine/Proton with an FSR hook; OpenNR's target is Windows SkyrimVR Feature 18 with exact per-eye resources.
rows.decision: Do not port the installer, modified vkd3d pair or ReShade bridge into the protected OpenNR/MGO route.

rows.evidence: The live route blocks on synchronous CPU staging, resets history each frame, and has no frame-generation support; no SkyrimVR headset test is supplied.
rows.decision: No temporal, stereo, headset, compositor or VR-budget claim follows from this repository.

rows.evidence: Project source and third-party notices are published, but the workflow converts a privately obtained NVIDIA DLL into coefficient tables and bundles modified runtime components.
rows.decision: Keep source and locally derived artifacts private; do not redistribute or package them without a separate ownership/terms review.

source.label: Crosswalk from external claims to OpenNR acceptance gates
filters: OpenNR promotion gates and protected Feature 18 route
External repository main snapshot and release v0.1.0-poc

metricDefinitions.label: Promotion=false
metricDefinitions.definition: The artifact may remain an isolated research reference but has not earned entry into the native teacher, student, runtime, package or deployment lineage.

rows.action: Keep the AMD HIP repository as a pinned read-only backend reference.
rows.reason: It validates the value of explicit family schedules, fused kernels, residual boundaries and strict provenance without requiring another data collection pass.
rows.stop_condition: Stop using it as evidence if a later revision removes its provenance caveats or changes the claimed graph without a matching source diff.

rows.action: Do not install or execute the Linux bridge on the protected MGO/OpenNR route.
rows.reason: The platform, hook ownership, GPU target, temporal behavior and resource contract do not match current SkyrimVR acceptance.
rows.stop_condition: No exception unless a separately authorized Linux/AMD target is added with its own backup, runtime and headset gates.

rows.action: Reuse the compact trace schema for selected local CUDA/recovered-graph boundaries.
rows.reason: Per-block counts, finiteness, range, sum and hash are useful low-volume health checks alongside the existing OpenNR stage traces.
rows.stop_condition: Do not call this feature distillation; add actual serialized activations only for explicitly selected stages.

rows.action: If feature distillation is pursued, add a small isolated activation-dump probe around the eight ViT blocks and one encoder/decoder boundary.
rows.reason: This can test whether internal supervision is more informative than final RGB matching, but only as an architecture probe against a named recovered lineage.
rows.stop_condition: Require source-matched native first-frame parity and sequence/eye/reset metadata before using outputs as teacher targets.

rows.action: Continue the existing native-style CUDA fusion and resolution study.
rows.reason: It is hardware-local to the RTX target and already has measured C32/C64/C128/C256/C512/global slices and native Feature 18 speed anchors.
rows.stop_condition: Require full-eye output parity, temporal state, stereo, Feature 18 ownership and live VR budget before any promotion.

rows.action: Do not collect broad new Skyrim data for this lead.
rows.reason: More images cannot repair derived layout uncertainty, absent activation dumps, an unfused runtime or a Linux/AMD platform mismatch.
rows.stop_condition: Collect only if a bounded feature probe or native-parity diagnosis identifies a specific missing visual regime.
